Name: Verification of compliant delivery devices operated by contracted delivery workers, and to repeal section 20-1526 of such code, relating to powered mobility devices of contracted delivery workers.
Title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to verification of compliant delivery devices operated by contracted delivery workers, and to repeal section 20-1526 of such code, relating to powered mobility devices of contracted delivery workers

History.Description: This Introduction was Introduced by Council
This Introduction was Referred to Comm by Council to the Committee on Consumer and Worker Protection
This Introduction was Re-referred to Committee by Council to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure

Summary: This bill would require delivery services to verify that the delivery devices used by their workers are in compliance with applicable law, rules, and regulations. Details about the verification process—including how often and in what manner such verification should be completed by the delivery services and be provided to the Department of Transportation (“DOT”)—would be specified by DOT rule. Delivery services that violate the verification requirements would be subject to a civil penalty, and those that commit 6 or more violations within a 2-year period could have their license suspended, revoked, or not renewed by the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection.
Text:
A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to verification of compliant delivery devices operated by contracted delivery workers, and to repeal section 20-1526 of such code, relating to powered mobility devices of contracted delivery workers

Be it enacted by the Council as follows:


Section 1. Section 20-1526 of the administrative code of the city of New York is REPEALED.
§ 2. Section 20-1501 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new definition of “delivery device” in alphabetical order to read as follows:
Delivery device. The term “delivery device” means a powered mobility device, or any other device or vehicle that is incapable of being registered with the department of motor vehicles.
§ 3. Title 19 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new chapter 13 to read as follows:
Chapter 13
DELIVERY DEVICES
§ 19-1301 Definitions. For purposes of this subchapter, the following terms have the following meanings:
Compliant delivery device. The term “compliant delivery device” has the same meaning as set forth in section 20-1501.
Contracted delivery worker. The term “contracted delivery worker” has the same meaning as set forth in section 20-1501.
Delivery device. The term “delivery device” has the same meaning as set forth in section 20-1501.
Delivery service. The term “delivery service” has the same meaning as set forth in section 20-1501.
Goods. The term “goods” has the same meaning as set forth in section 20-1501.
Trip. The term “trip” has the same meaning as set forth in section 20-1501.
§ 19-1302 Compliant delivery devices. a. A delivery service may not offer or assign a trip to a contracted delivery worker unless it has verified that the delivery device used by such contracted delivery worker to deliver goods on behalf of such delivery service is a compliant delivery device and provided proof of such verification to the department. A delivery service shall continually verify, and provide proof of such verification, as set forth in the rules of the department, that contracted delivery workers being offered or assigned trips by the delivery service are using compliant delivery devices.
b. The department shall promulgate rules for the implementation of this section, provided that such rules shall specify:
1. How frequently delivery services shall continually verify, and provide proof of such verification, that contracted delivery workers being offered or assigned trips by the delivery service are using compliant delivery devices;
2. The manner in which delivery services conduct such verification, including but not limited to requiring delivery services to notify contracted delivery workers of the requirement to use a compliant delivery device, and the process for verifying that contracted delivery workers are using a compliant delivery device; and
3. The format in which delivery services shall provide proof of such verification to the department.
c. Penalties. 1. A delivery service that violates subdivision b or any rule promulgated pursuant to subdivision b shall be liable for a civil penalty as follows:
(a) For a first violation, a penalty of $500; and
(b) For a second or subsequent violation issued within a period of 30 days, a penalty of $1,000.
2. Civil penalties issued pursuant to paragraph 1 shall be recoverable in an action in any court of competent jurisdiction or in a proceeding before the office of administrative trials and hearings.
§ 4. Section 20-563.9 of the administrative code of the city of New York, as amended by local law number 133 for the year 2025, is amended by adding a new subdivision g to read as follows:
g. Committed six or more violations of any provision of subdivision a of section 19-1302 or of any rule promulgated by the department of transportation pursuant to subdivision b of such section within a 2 year period.
§ 5. This local law takes effect 3 years after it becomes law.
